intro.data: Encode packs the file. To undo it you need a decoder that returns the EXACT original. Two decoders are offered — one restores the file, the other returns something corrupted. Encode, then pick the true inverse.
intro.alchemy: Grind turns the bar to dust. To undo it you need a recast that returns the EXACT original. Two are offered — one restores the bar, the other returns something impure. Grind, then pick the true inverse.
intro.spellcraft: Etch turns the sigil to a glyph. To undo it you need a reading that returns the EXACT original. Two are offered — one restores the sigil, the other returns something broken. Etch, then pick the true inverse.
intro.abstract: f maps A→B. Pick the g : B→A whose round trip returns the original value, not a corrupted one.

goal.data: Encode, then decode back to the very same file you started with.
goal.alchemy: Grind, then recast back to the very same bar.
goal.spellcraft: Etch, then read back to the very same sigil.
goal.abstract: Round-trip back to the original value.

description.data: packs the data into a blob
description.spellcraft: etches the spark into a glyph

description.abstract: B → A, but not an inverse

afterSuccess.data: Decode brought back the exact original — encoding then decoding changed nothing. Garble was the same type but returned a corrupted file, so it is no inverse. g ∘ f = id_A holds only for the true decoder.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Recast brought back the exact bar. Miscast returned something impure, so it is no inverse. g ∘ f = id_A holds only for the true recast.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Reading brought back the exact sigil. Misreading returned something broken, so it is no inverse. g ∘ f = id_A holds only for the true reading.
afterSuccess.abstract: The true inverse returned the original: g ∘ f = id_A. The look-alike corrupted it.

reveal.summary: An inverse must return you to the exact starting value. When g ∘ f = id_A, g is a left inverse of f — verified here by running the round trip.
reveal.moreFormal: A left inverse g of f : A → B satisfies g ∘ f = id_A. Same type as a real inverse is not enough — it must actually restore every value.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: decode(encode(x)) === x — a lossy 'decoder' fails this.
